Issue 2: Lacers clashing with couplers.

See adjacent picture #1 showing the on-site situation. Couplers of BM227 were cast in 45mm out of position towards the outer edge of the Reactor Pit. Resulting in a gap too small for the lacers line 2 to fit between them.

NOTE: BYLOR used bridging coupler on the 4No. C40 to allow the line 1 of lacers to fit (picture #2_. Can this solution be reviewed by JDO as well please. 
Removing the Bridging couplers would shift this clash down from line 2 to line 1.

The C40 coupler to install is 170mm height.
In this space of 320mm (yellow dashed area picture #3), from the bottom of the Bridging Sleeves installed to the top of the Male couplers of BM227, no lacers from line 2 (BM115 + BM118) can fit between the vertical couplers (picture #4).

answer:
Solution 1 (photo #1 opposite): BYLOR propose to shift out of position line 2 of FF3 to the line 3 position. It will result leaving a gap between line 1 and new line 2 of 320mm (352mm centre to centre). Line 3 will be lifted as much as BYLOR can achieve on site. The gap between the adjacent layers would be 20mm.

Solution 2 (photo #2 opposite): BYLOR propose to shift HRX-04/Zone16/115 and HRX-04/Zone16/118 from FF3 to FF5. This will result to shift those 2No. bars by 72mm. It will be on layer FF5 only in this area, the tips of the bar would start and end in FF3.

Solution 3 (photo #3 opposite):
BYLOR propose to rotate the whole line 2 so that the lap is shifted out of the clashing area.

Then, BYLOR propose to cut 650mm of the clashing part of BM115. BYLOR will rotate the whole line 2 so that it leaves 1200mm length before the lap of C32. This solution allows the steel to stay in FF3, and the missing C32 section being replaced by the 4No. additional C16.
